concepts.why: The presence of a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice suggest Tricuspid Atresia.
The presence of a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects suggest Ventricular Septal Defect.

The combination of cyanosis, a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle, and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects suggest Tetralogy of Fallot.
The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects suggest Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
